text.p: Shares in French carmaker Renault SA gave back some of last week's gains as investors took profits on Monday and amid concerns of a prolonged strike, traders and analysts said.
The stock should, however, resume rising again in the near term, following last Thursday's announcement of plans to close a Belgian assembly plant, analysts said.
Renault was down 4.83 percent at 139.8 francs at 1330 GMT, while the market was up 0.41 percent. The company was brought to the market in 1994 at 170 francs per share.
One analyst said he expected the stock to climb back to 170 in the near term. "This morning's retreat does not worry me," he said.

"The big problem in the auto sector is overcapacity, a problem which no-one has dared to touch for 20 years for obvious labour reasons," he added. "The fact that Renault is tackling it is a good sign."
Another analyst said, "At the worst, there will be a strike and the share will fall but the strike will not go on forever."

Renault unions have called for a one-hour stoppage for Friday in factories in France, Belgium and Spain, to protest the closure of the Vilvoorde plant, near Brussels, which will cost 3,100 jobs and save 825 million French francs a year .
An industry source said Renault is due to announce somewhat fewer than 3,000 job losses in France this year.
